extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs; Department/agency administrators and policy-makers
extracted.subtask_description: An 1879–80 U.S. Indian agent annual report describing reservation administration (population, agriculture, schools, police, infrastructure, and recommendations). Provides operational measures, policy recommendations, and indicators of progress for agency management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health and vital statistics reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of Indians who have received medical treatment during the past year was 446. Number of births, 99. Number of deaths, 68. This record is believed to be correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and report accurate counts of medical treatments, births, and deaths for the agency population; explicitly state confidence in records. Use these figures to evaluate public-health activity and medical staff workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Livestock accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: A careful count of live stock owned by Indians has been taken ... approximate result: 850 horses and 2,600 head of cattle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out regular inventories of horses, cattle, and other stock; report approximate totals and use counts to assess pastoral capacity and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: School capacity and attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Saint John's boarding and industrial school, for girls, ... average attendance of 20 scholars, all that could be accommodated. Recent improvements ... permit the number to be increased to 30. Two day-schools ... were carried on with fair success. At other school buildings, either from lack of teachers or scholars, there has been little or no school in operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate schools by capacity, average attendance, and availability of teachers; prioritize reopening or staffing industrial/boarding schools when teachers are assigned; consider physical improvements to expand capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural acreage and breaking recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to break up by contract five to ten acres for each family. The season for breaking new land in time to have it planted is so short in the spring that it was impossible to do more without neglecting the necessary work of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote breaking new land by contract (5–10 acres per family) to increase cultivated acreage; plan breaking early because of a short spring window; compare acreage year-to-year to measure advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ration discontinuation conditional on tribal production
rubrics_metrics.description: I gave the Indians notice that the issue of corn would be discontinued and stopped the ration, as they had raised enough for their own use last year and would be expected to do so in the future. Next year I think enough of wheat can be produced to supply the tribe with flour. To do this, however, a grist-mill and bolting apparatus will be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cease rations when local production (corn/wheat) suffices for subsistence; ensure necessary processing infrastructure (grist-mill, bolting apparatus) is available to move from rations to local flour production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency farm allocation and production targets
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency farm ... Eight acres of it was parceled out to Indians who could not get breaking done in time to plant. The area planted was as follows: Wheat 41 acres; Oats 70 acres; Corn 25 acres; Potatoes 4 acres; Employes' garden 3 acres; Total 143 acres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use agency farm to produce seed, forage, and hay (e.g., 150 tons of hay reported) and to support tribe and employees; parcel small plots to families unable to break land themselves; hire temporary labor for harvest and hay-making and assist infirm individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological record keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly table of daily mean, maximum, minimum temperatures and rainfall (e.g., daily means for months and highest 103°, lowest -40°). Height above sea level 1,440 feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain monthly meteorological records (mean/max/min temperature, precipitation), record extremes and elevation; use climate data to plan agricultural timing and crop choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of livestock conditional on assurance of care
rubrics_metrics.description: During the year occasional issues of cattle and swine were made to individuals who asked for them and gave satisfactory assurance of their ability to take proper care of them; and in June the three hundred head of domestic cattle purchased by the department for the tribe were issued to them in accordance with instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue stock only to individuals who provide satisfactory assurances of care; monitor pasturage suitability and animal losses; encourage improvement of equine stock (replace pony with American horse, cross-breeding) and proper herding practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land in severalty allotment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: While I consider that the very great majority of the Sioux are unprepared to acquire land in severalty, I believe the experiment can be now safely made with this tribe. I deem it to be worse than useless to confer upon an Indian just emerging from barbarism the maximum of 320 acres of land in fee simple, as contemplated by the law; 160 acres is wholly sufficient and admits double the number to a share in the choicest tracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage allotment in severalty cautiously; prefer 160-acre allotments over 320-acre maximums to enable broader distribution; be aware of legal vulnerabilities of Indian freehold without civil rights and protect titles against seizure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of civilization/progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The independence of the family, the exclusive title of the individual in personal property and chattels, the submission of disputes to arbitration, the merit and respectability of manual labor, occupation of comfortable and healthful abodes, increasing engagement in manual labor, apprenticeships, houses erected, and issuance of household furniture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure 'civilization' progress by family independence, property ownership, dispute arbitration, respectable manual labor, housing quality (frame/shingled/floored/double windows), apprenticeships completed, and distribution of household furniture to industrious families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation of dances and cultural practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Indians ... have abandoned the most immoral and objectionable dances. The 'Grass Dance' is still retained. Dancing is not prohibited but is restricted to Saturday afternoons and evenings, after the hours of labor. It would be unwise to assail a superstitious prejudice by force, without the power to totally destroy or eradicate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulate (rather than prohibit) traditional practices to maintain peace and order: restrict timing (e.g., Saturdays after labor hours), avoid forcible eradication which can provoke disputes, and seek compromise to preserve social harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education modality and isolation during instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The camp schools were closed ... The industrial school has just been closed in consequence of a contemplated change in the management. I recommend that for the present the industrial school only be maintained. It is of the first importance that Indian children, during the period of instruction, be isolated wholly from the tribe, and dwell exclusively amid the surroundings of civilized life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer industrial/boarding school models over scattered day schools when teachers and returns are scarce; isolate pupils from tribal environment during instruction to maximize assimilation and attendance, especially where families live far apart or in inclement weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionary staffing and native clergy
rubrics_metrics.description: The influence of an earnest missionary effort ... is undoubtedly very beneficial. Unfortunately this is rarely the case, attention being generally given to devotional exercises ... while the practical part of Christianity is mostly neglected. If educated native clergymen could be obtained for this work it would be an inestimable boon to the Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff missionary efforts with educated native clergymen and emphasize practical aspects of religion to increase beneficial influence; avoid purely devotional programs unintelligible to Indians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian police organization and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The police force consists of one captain, one sergeant, and eight privates. It is very efficient ... gives great assistance by carrying messages to distant parts of the reservation, watching freight at the landing, recovering stray animals, etc. The arms sent out by the department for the police force have been given to them and are kept in excellent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize a local police with clear rank structure and standing orders; assign duties (messaging, freight/watch, animal recovery); keep arms and equipment in order; use police to enforce orders and support agency administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance and dispute-resolution procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Every violation of rule, or misconduct, requiring censure or punishment, is promptly reported to the office and the offender brought to account. My office presents the appearance of a police court, sometimes consuming a whole day ... plaintiff, defendant and witnesses being summoned ... Decisions given at the office are accepted as final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use police-assisted hearings (police court) on public days to hear disputes (trespass, damages, false reports, joint labor claims); summon parties and witnesses; promptly report punishments to central office; accept that some offenses may be overlooked or condoned but require formal reporting of serious cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation monitoring and land-title vigilance
rubrics_metrics.description: The reservation comprises over 322,000 acres ... The two greatest railroads pass along its boundaries ... it will not be long until a demand will be made for the cession of this land ... It is believed that, by finding some defect in the title, the Winnebago and possibly the Sioux tracts may be recovered from the Indians and opened to settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor railroad/settler encroachment and political pressure for cession; scrutinize historical title issues and prepare to defend tribal land from legal challenges; anticipate and report land-security risks to the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency infrastructure maintenance and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency buildings number 25 ... Several buildings that were useless and a nuisance have been removed. A warehouse 100 feet by 40 was erected, and a small building for postmaster and telegraph operator put up ... An additional warehouse and a stable and granary will be constructed; an office and employes' dwelling are now being constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey and remove unsafe/nuisance structures; prioritize construction of warehouses, granaries, stables, offices, and employee housing; allocate lumber and labor for necessary repairs; clean up accumulations and debris from long neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment composition and labor planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The employe force consist of—Whites: 1 clerk, 1 physician, 1 storekeeper, 1 farmer, 1 blacksmith, 2 carpenters, 1 chief herder, 5 laborers. Indians: 1 interpreter, 4 apprentices, 3 herders, 6 laborers. Indians are employed for irregular labor when needed, harvest-ing, making hay, cutting lumber, hauling freight, and casual labor about the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff agencies with a mix of clerical, skilled, and ordinary labor; employ Indian labor for seasonal tasks; plan supplies and labor a year in advance for widely dispersed families; use interpreters but recognize their limits; anticipate rapidly increasing administrative workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation and economic self-sufficiency metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: All wagon transportation for this agency is done by the Indians of reservation ... they have hauled 960,955 pounds of freight during the year, saving government funds and earning payments from the Quartermaster Department (dollar amounts provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track pounds hauled, distances, payments received, and savings to government to measure economic activity and self-help; use freight work as income and training for Indians; record and report detailed transport metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship training and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: One blacksmith's apprentice (Saul Demans) and one carpenter's apprentice (James Williams) have finished their apprenticeship and become fairly efficient workmen. Elsewhere: six young men learning trades ... have progressed satisfactorily; two have about three years' experience and are quite handy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish apprenticeships in trades (blacksmithing, carpentry); monitor progress and duration; report completion and competency; use apprenticeships to create skilled labor within the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural equipment and suitability guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: There are also 2 grain-seeders, 25 harrows, 6 mowing-machines, 2 reapers, and 1 thrashing-machine upon the reservation, ... with the saw-mill now in use and the grist-mill in course of erection. This section is not adapted to stock-raising; short summers and long severe winters preclude stock-raising being profitable. Each family should have from one to four milk cows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate agricultural equipment and mills; prefer cultivation and cereal/vegetable production over large-scale stock-raising in climates with short summers; advise limited milk-cow ownership per family (1–4) to support learning and sustainability.
